шум.text: Borrowed from Middle High German schūm, from Old High German scūm, from Proto-Germanic *skūmaz. Cognate with English scum, German Schaum.

sources.quote: Borrowed from Polish nikczemny. With -ний (-nyj) suffix. Compare Russian никчёмный (nikčómnyj), Belarusian нікчэ́мны (nikčémny).

нікчемний.text: Borrowed from Polish nikczemny. With -ний (-nyj) suffix. Compare Russian никчёмный (nikčómnyj), Belarusian нікчэ́мны (nikčémny).

sources.quote: Inherited from Old Ruthenian ꙋкропъ (ukrop, “hot water”), from Old East Slavic ꙋкропъ (ukropŭ, “hot water”), from Proto-Slavic *ukropъ. Cognate with Old Church Slavonic оукропъ (ukropŭ, “hot soup”) and Czech úkrop (“garlic soup”).

окріп.text: Inherited from Old Ruthenian ꙋкропъ (ukrop, “hot water”), from Old East Slavic ꙋкропъ (ukropŭ, “hot water”), from Proto-Slavic *ukropъ. Cognate with Old Church Slavonic оукропъ (ukropŭ, “hot soup”) and Czech úkrop (“garlic soup”).
